title: Delivery Performance Domain
coreMove: Treat delivery as a live domain: trace each output through requirements, scope, quality, acceptance, and value before calling the work healthy.

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads who treat delivery as final handoff
exampleSpecs.stakes: a green delivery column hides weak acceptance evidence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Therese reframes Delivery Performance Domain as a live link from output to value within the 8 domains

exampleSpecs.audience: learners meeting performance domains for the first time
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusion turns useful signals into paperwork
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Dmytro learns that requirements, scope, quality, and acceptance criteria are delivery signals

exampleSpecs.audience: release leads relying on output counts
exampleSpecs.stakes: a green board hides weak stakeholder use
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jasper reviews the same process before and after adding requirements, scope, quality, and acceptance criteria

exampleSpecs.audience: reviewers checking why accepted work failed in use
exampleSpecs.stakes: records show activity but not delivery health
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Garrett finds the telling detail in requirements, scope, quality, and acceptance criteria records

exampleSpecs.audience: product owners tempted by simple delivery counts
exampleSpecs.stakes: a high output number may hide poor outcome evidence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Whitney works through the wrong turns inside her head before tracing outputs to acceptance and outcomes

exampleSpecs.audience: project managers with scarce review time
exampleSpecs.stakes: limited attention must cover delivery signals and domain interactions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maeva allocates scarce attention across the 8 domains before any review action begins
